genZNote: Lives happily in boiling-hot, battery-acid-pH volcanic springs — the kind of place that would dissolve almost anything else alive.

morphology.notes: Thrives at ~75-80°C and pH ~2-3, oxidizing elemental sulfur for energy in some strains.

habitat.naturalHabitat: Acidic volcanic hot springs and sulfur-rich geothermal environments
habitat.environmentalOccurrence: Found worldwide in geothermal areas such as Yellowstone's acidic sulfur springs

microscopy.stain: Not Gram-stained routinely; specialized wet mount

culture.growthCharacteristics: Grows optimally at ~75-80°C and pH ~2-3; will not grow at neutral pH or moderate temperature
culture.colonyMorphology: Not routinely characterized by colony morphology; studied mainly in liquid culture

identificationClues: Requires both extreme heat (~75-80°C) and extreme acidity (pH ~2-3) simultaneously — a true thermoacidophile
Irregular, lobed coccoid cell shape distinguishes it microscopically from typical bacterial cocci
An archaeon studied as a model organism for understanding life's upper limits of temperature and pH tolerance
Not associated with any human or animal disease

examFacts.keyBiochemicalReaction: Growth requires high temperature (~75-80°C) and low pH (~2-3)
examFacts.importantTest: Growth only under combined extreme heat and acidity
examFacts.distinguishingFeature: Classic thermoacidophilic archaeon from volcanic hot springs, illustrating the outer limits of habitable conditions for life
